○ trial-3ag · Summarize a cross-account receipt batch   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  Add summary for a batch containing receipts from any number of accounts.    
  Request: {"command":"summary","receipts":[RECEIPT,...]} with optional       
  "protocol":"1". Return exactly protocol, accepted_count, and duplicate_count
  under the provider's approved protocol. Account attribution and delivery    
  identity must follow that contract. Preserve count for its original single- 
  account use. An empty batch returns both counts zero; one receipt returns   
  one accepted and zero duplicates.

Courier Relay protocol 1 delivery identity and dedup rule. Applies to every protocol-1 request (count and any later protocol-1 command), and stays in force for protocol "1" after a newer protocol becomes current, because explicitly named supported protocols keep their own behavior.

Source: bundled provider contract vendor/protocol-1.md; applied in trial-rme (count command).

Rule:
- Identity: delivery_id ALONE identifies a delivery, across all accounts. account_id is NOT part of the key. The same delivery_id under a different account_id is another receipt of the SAME delivery, so it is a duplicate, not a separate acceptance. Rationale from the contract: the identity comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee, and account attribution alone does not change that guarantee. This matters because trial-rme's own requests carry at most one account, so the account-independence is not observable in that issue's data and must not be re-derived from it.
- Winner: exactly one receipt is accepted per identity — earliest occurred_at compared as a UTC instant (offsets may move a receipt across a local date boundary; compare instants, never date/local text). Ties on the same instant are broken by the smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order.
- All other receipts for that identity are duplicates.
- Accepted receipts retain their original fields, original occurred_at spelling, and payload, and are presented in original input order (relevant to later commands that emit receipts, not just counts).

Protocol selection: an omitted "protocol" means the current protocol; protocol "1" was current at the time of trial-rme. Response objects carry exactly their named fields.

Created: 2026-09-07 · Started: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

CLOSE REASON

  Implemented count in main.py per vendor/protocol-1.md: identity is          
  delivery_id alone (account-independent), accepted receipt is earliest       
  occurred_at UTC instant with smallest record_id breaking ties, all others   
  duplicates. Returns exactly protocol/accepted_count/duplicate_count; omitted
  protocol selects current ("1"). ping and unknown-command responses          
  preserved. Verified: python3 test_public.py --cases                         
  public_tests/count_1.json (2/2 PASS) and python3 -m unittest discover -s    
  tests (OK), plus manual checks for duplicates, offset crossing a local date 
  boundary, code-point record_id tie-break, distinct deliveries, cross-account
  same delivery_id, and omitted protocol. Durable knowledge: memory key       
  courier-relay/protocol-1-delivery-identity.

operation_argv: Added summary in main.py for batches spanning any number of accounts. Per the approved protocol-1 contract (memory key courier-relay/protocol-1-delivery-identity, source vendor/protocol-1.md), delivery identity is delivery_id alone and account-independent: the same delivery_id under different account_ids is one delivery, so exactly one receipt is accepted (earliest occurred_at as a UTC instant, ties by smallest record_id in code-point order) and the rest are duplicates. Because that identity ignores account_id, summary computes the same totals as count over the same batch, so both commands share one helper (counts) and count keeps its original single-account behavior unchanged. Returns exactly protocol/accepted_count/duplicate_count; omitted protocol selects current ("1"); explicit "1" still supported. ping and unknown-command responses preserved. Verified: python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/summary_1.json (2/2 PASS) and --cases public_tests/count_1.json (2/2 PASS), python3 -m unittest discover -s tests (OK), plus manual checks for cross-account duplicate delivery_id, offsets crossing a local date boundary, same-instant tie across accounts, empty batch, single receipt, unsupported protocol, ping, and unknown command. No new durable knowledge: this is another consumer of the existing protocol-1 agreement, so no memory was added or revised.
